question: What inspectable Lake Bito fish-study evidence is available, and can the 2023 thesis and 2025 conference abstract be counted as independent surveys?

waterbody.name: Lake Bito
waterbody.disambiguation: This is Lake Bito in MacArthur, Leyte. Keep separate from Lake Bato in Camarines Sur, Lake Bito-on in other localities, and Lake Danao in Ormoc City.
waterbody.geometryDecision: No coordinates or geometry added. The reviewed thesis listing, conference abstract, and hydrology record do not provide fish station coordinates or an authoritative lake boundary.

2023ThesisListing.citation: Tenio, K. F. C. (2023). Water Quality, Fish Communities, and Land Cover Analysis of Lake Bito in MacArthur, Leyte, Philippines. MS Environmental Science thesis, University of the Philippines Los Baños, as listed in the SESAM Library theses index.
2023ThesisListing.evidenceAvailable: The public index entry reports water-quality, fish-abundance, participatory-rural-appraisal and land-cover work; 354 freshwater fish from eight families and nine species; and a very low diversity index of 0.37. It does not name the fish taxa or provide the full thesis, sampling dates, gear, station allocation, vouchers or sample identifiers in the reviewed entry.
2023ThesisListing.retrievalStatus: Public thesis-index PDF and indexed abstract text reviewed; thesis full text and underlying data not retrieved.

2025ConferenceAbstract.citation: Tenio, K. F. C., Cui, L. E., Camacho, M. V., Villanueva-Peyraube, J., & Guotana, J. M. R. (2025). Investigating the Status of Lake Bito: Water Quality, Fish Communities, and Land Cover Analysis in MacArthur, Leyte, Philippines. EM-16-88, 16th International Conference on Environmental and Rural Development Book of Abstracts, p. 116.
2025ConferenceAbstract.evidenceAvailable: The abstract names Lake Bito in MacArthur, Leyte and reports 354 freshwater fish, eight families and nine species, diversity index 0.37, seasonal variation in pH/BOD/DO, and an omnivorous forage characterization at the community level. It gives no species names, fish-level diet observations, sampling dates/methods, vouchers or station locations.
2025ConferenceAbstract.relationshipTo2023Thesis: Likely the same underlying project or thesis results re-presented: the first author and core subject match, and the identical specimen total, family count, species count and diversity index are unusually specific. The abstract does not explicitly identify itself as derived from the thesis, and no sample-level crosswalk was found. Retain both publication records but treat them as one likely underlying survey for inventory counting unless primary records establish otherwise.

2013HydrologyContext.citation: Jocson, T. C., & Costim, E. Y. (2013). Hydrological features of Lakes Bito, Mahagnao, and Danao in Leyte. In LakeCon2011: Building on the pillars of Integrated Lake Basin Management (Second National Congress on Philippine Lakes), pp. 298-300. PCAARRD-DOST.
2013HydrologyContext.evidenceAvailable: The SEAFDEC repository abstract identifies Lake Bito as a 126-hectare lake under MacArthur, Leyte jurisdiction and reports that the study context included Nile tilapia fish pens/cages and open-water fishery. It describes one year of monthly hydrological measurements. It does not provide an inspectable fish-species list or fish-station evidence in the repository abstract.
2013HydrologyContext.roleBoundary: Location, historical lake-use and environmental-study context only; not a fish inventory, present-day water-quality statement, legal-access guide or safety advisory.

decision.diet: The conference abstract describes an omnivorous community-level forage pattern, not species-specific natural diets or local gut-content results; no diet card added.
decision.reason: The accessible thesis listing and abstract contain only aggregate fish counts; taxon names, methods, effort, site-level evidence, vouchers and item-specific reuse terms remain unavailable.

limits: The repeated aggregate results support a likely thesis/conference version relationship but do not prove exact specimen identity or eliminate the possibility of later additions; do not combine them as independent surveys by default.
Nine species is an aggregate study-reported count, not an extractable checklist. No names may be inferred from the 2013 tilapia aquaculture context or community forage description.
The 2013 SEAFDEC item is a conference paper metadata/abstract record; it reports hydrological measurements and lake use, not a species-by-site fish record.

Historical study-period water quality cannot establish current safety. A 2012-2013 fish-kill/news report, if reviewed, must remain a dated incident record and cannot support a present-day warning without current official monitoring.
No source absence is evidence that Lake Bito contains no other fish or that no fuller dataset exists.
nextAction: Search official VSU/UPLB repositories and public specimen catalogs for Tenio's full thesis, species list, methods, voucher accessions and item-specific reuse terms. If unavailable, retain Lake Bito as an unresolved high-value study lead and continue the Eastern Visayas freshwater sweep without treating the abstract aggregate as a checklist.
